name: Moses, and the Egyptian in the sand
charge: Slaying the Egyptian that smote his brother, and hiding him in the sand
summary: Raised in Pharaoh’s house but nursed by his own mother, Moses always knew who he was. At forty it came into his heart to visit his brethren, and he looked on their burdens and saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew and killed him. He did not merely marvel at the oppression; he used his position for his people, supposing his brethren would understand that God would deliver them by his hand. They did not understand, the man in the wrong threw the killing in his face, and Moses fled to Midian a stranger in a strange land forty years, until the God of his fathers sent back the man they had refused.
offenseFull: A man of the house of Levi took to wife a daughter of Levi, Amram and Jochebed, and the child was goodly, exceeding fair; by faith his parents hid him three months and were not afraid of the king’s commandment (Exodus 2:1-2; Exodus 6:20; Acts 7:20; Hebrews 11:23). Pharaoh’s daughter drew him out of the river and knew at once that this was one of the Hebrews’ children, because the Most High puts a difference between the Egyptians and Israel, though both peoples were dark of skin (Exodus 2:5-6; Exodus 11:7). His sister Miriam was crafty, and by her offer his own mother was called and paid wages to nurse him, so that his first years were spent with her (Exodus 2:7-9). He was raised in the royal court and received one of the finest educations in the world, learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and mighty in words and in deeds (Acts 7:22).

When he was full forty years old it came into his heart to visit his brethren, the children of Israel; he went out to them and looked on their burdens, and he spied an Egyptian smiting a Hebrew, one of his brethren (Exodus 2:11; Acts 7:23). He did not act as though the palace had made him something else. This was not ordinary correction on a work site; it was an abuse of power in which his brother’s life was in danger. He looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he slew the Egyptian and hid him in the sand (Exodus 2:12). He did not kill out of hatred, and the law weighs the other side of it: if a man forbears to deliver them that are drawn to death and those that are ready to be slain, and says he did not know it, the one that ponders the heart considers it, and he that keeps the soul knows it, and renders to every man according to his works (Proverbs 24:11-12). He did not merely marvel at the matter as the preacher warns (Ecclesiastes 5:8); he used his position for his people, supposing his brethren would have understood that God by his hand would deliver them, but they did not understand (Acts 7:25).

The second day two men of the Hebrews strove together, and he asked the one that did the wrong why he smote his fellow. The man answered by asking who made him a prince and a judge over them, and whether he meant to kill him as he had killed the Egyptian (Exodus 2:13-14). When a people is oppressed they take the oppression out on one another, and the same spirit answers correction among our people now, pointing the finger at the one who corrects. Moses was afraid, and knew that the thing was known.
judgmentFull: When Pharaoh heard of it he sought to slay Moses, but Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh and dwelt in the land of Midian (Exodus 2:15). By faith he refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter, choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season, esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures of Egypt (Hebrews 11:24-26). At the well he stood up for the seven daughters of the priest of Midian against the shepherds and watered their flock, a man of war and not a weak man, and they told their father that an Egyptian had delivered them, for Moses was a very dark-skinned man, the same colour as the Egyptians (Exodus 2:16-19). He married Zipporah and named his son Gershom, because he had been a stranger in a strange land (Exodus 2:21-22).

No sentence upon the killing is recorded. Forty years later, at eighty, the angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire in a bush at Sinai, and the man they had refused with the question, who made him a ruler and a judge over them, is the same man God sent to be a ruler and a deliverer (Acts 7:30-35). The people he had tried to help turned on him; the God of his fathers sent him back to deliver them.

text.text: And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi.
And the woman conceived, and bare a son: and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months.
And Amram took him Jochebed his father’s sister to wife; and she bare him Aaron and Moses: and the years of the life of Amram were an hundred and thirty and seven years.
In which time Moses was born, and was exceeding fair, and nourished up in his father’s house three months:
By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months of his parents, because they saw he was a proper child; and they were not afraid of the king’s commandment.
And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash herself at the river; and her maidens walked along by the river’s side; and when she saw the ark among the flags, she sent her maid to fetch it.
And when she had opened it, she saw the child: and, behold, the babe wept. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews’ children.
But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.
Then said his sister to Pharaoh’s daughter, Shall I go and call to thee a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for thee?
And Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, Go. And the maid went and called the child’s mother.
And Pharaoh’s daughter said unto her, Take this child away, and nurse it for me, and I will give thee thy wages. And the woman took the child, and nursed it.
And Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds.
And it came to pass in those days, when Moses was grown, that he went out unto his brethren, and looked on their burdens: and he spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren.
And when he was full forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Israel.
And he looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he slew the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.
If thou forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain;

If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?

If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter: for he that is higher than the highest regardeth; and there be higher than they.
For he supposed his brethren would have understood how that God by his hand would deliver them: but they understood not.
And when he went out the second day, behold, two men of the Hebrews strove together: and he said to him that did the wrong, Wherefore smitest thou thy fellow?
And he said, Who made thee a prince and a judge over us? intendest thou to kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian? And Moses feared, and said, Surely this thing is known.
Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian: and he sat down by a well.
By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter;
Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season;
Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward.
Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters: and they came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father’s flock.
And the shepherds came and drove them away: but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock.
And when they came to Reuel their father, he said, How is it that ye are come so soon to day?
And they said, An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and also drew water enough for us, and watered the flock.
And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.
And she bare him a son, and he called his name Gershom: for he said, I have been a stranger in a strange land.
And when forty years were expired, there appeared to him in the wilderness of mount Sina an angel of the Lord in a flame of fire in a bush.
When Moses saw it, he wondered at the sight: and as he drew near to behold it, the voice of the Lord came unto him,
Saying, I am the God of thy fathers, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. Then Moses trembled, and durst not behold.
Then said the Lord to him, Put off thy shoes from thy feet: for the place where thou standest is holy ground.
I have seen, I have seen the affliction of my people which is in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning, and am come down to deliver them. And now come, I will send thee into Egypt.
This Moses whom they refused, saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge? the same did God send to be a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the angel which appeared to him in the bush.
And it came to pass in those days, when Moses was grown, that he went out unto his brethren, and looked on their burdens: and he spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren.
And he looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he slew the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.
And when he went out the second day, behold, two men of the Hebrews strove together: and he said to him that did the wrong, Wherefore smitest thou thy fellow?
And he said, Who made thee a prince and a judge over us? intendest thou to kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian? And Moses feared, and said, Surely this thing is known.
Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian: and he sat down by a well.
And seeing one of them suffer wrong, he defended him, and avenged him that was oppressed, and smote the Egyptian:
For he supposed his brethren would have understood how that God by his hand would deliver them: but they understood not.
And the next day he shewed himself unto them as they strove, and would have set them at one again, saying, Sirs, ye are brethren; why do ye wrong one to another?
But he that did his neighbour wrong thrust him away, saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge over us?
Wilt thou kill me, as thou diddest the Egyptian yesterday?
Then fled Moses at this saying, and was a stranger in the land of Madian, where he begat two sons.
In which time Moses was born, and was exceeding fair, and nourished up in his father’s house three months:
And when he was cast out, Pharaoh’s daughter took him up, and nourished him for her own son.
And Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds.
And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash herself at the river; and her maidens walked along by the river’s side; and when she saw the ark among the flags, she sent her maid to fetch it.
And when she had opened it, she saw the child: and, behold, the babe wept. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews’ children.
Then said his sister to Pharaoh’s daughter, Shall I go and call to thee a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for thee?
And Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, Go. And the maid went and called the child’s mother.
And Pharaoh’s daughter said unto her, Take this child away, and nurse it for me, and I will give thee thy wages. And the woman took the child, and nursed it.
Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian: and he sat down by a well.
Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters: and they came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father’s flock.
And the shepherds came and drove them away: but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock.
And when they came to Reuel their father, he said, How is it that ye are come so soon to day?
And they said, An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and also drew water enough for us, and watered the flock.
And he said unto his daughters, And where is he? why is it that ye have left the man? call him, that he may eat bread.
And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.
And she bare him a son, and he called his name Gershom: for he said, I have been a stranger in a strange land.
